name: The Couch household
head: couch_ira

arrival.note: The year the Couches bought the Tremont, which is the earliest date either source puts them at Chicago. It is a purchase date standing in for an arrival date and it is graded accordingly.

party_size_on_arrival.note: Two brothers are named in the purchase. Whether they travelled together, and whether either brought a family, is not stated.

reason_for_coming.value: To buy and run a hotel in a booming town
reason_for_coming.note: The purchase itself is documented; the motive is the obvious reading of it.

lives_at.note: A hotel proprietor of this period lived in his house. Not stated.

present_on_scene_date.note: Running the house across the scene date.

persons.name: Ira Couch

occupation.note: Proprietor of the first Tremont House. Andreas: 'the Couch brothers purchased the property and Ira Couch opened it as a hotel. He ran it until 1836, when his brother James took control.'

persons.note: 1 JULY 1835 FALLS SQUARELY INSIDE HIS TENURE, on two sources that do not disagree: chicagology's 1874 letter has him becoming proprietor in 1834, and Andreas has him running the house until 1836.

persons.name: James Couch

occupation.note: Andreas's phrase is 'the Couch brothers purchased the property', which makes James a partner in the house from the purchase; he did not take control until 1836. What he was doing in it on 1 July 1835 is not stated.

persons.note: A REAL, NAMED MAN WHOSE PRESENCE ON THE SCENE DATE IS THE RECONSTRUCTED PART. Andreas names him twice - as one of 'the Couch brothers' who bought the property and as the brother who took control in 1836 - and quotes him directly on how crowded the house was in its early days ('every available space of floor room' occupied at night). That he was living at Chicago in July 1835 rather than joining later is this project's reading of a joint purchase, not a statement in the source.

research_note: THE TREMONT'S FIRST PROPRIETOR, AND A CLEAN EXAMPLE OF THE derived GRADE DOING WORK. Ira Couch is documented in the house across 1 July 1835 by two independent sources. His brother James is a real, named man, documented as a co-purchaser and later as the proprietor, whose residence at Chicago on the scene date is reconstructed from the joint purchase rather than stated. Two men, two grades, one household. THE BUILDING THIS HOUSEHOLD IS ATTACHED TO IS THE FIRST TREMONT at Lake and Dearborn, built in 1833 by Alanson Sweet - not the later houses of 1840 and 1850 that carry the same name.

directories.note: LATER EVIDENCE, BESIDE THE 1835 CLAIMS AND NOT INSIDE THEM. A Chicago directory of 1839, 1843 or 1844 meets somebody of this name and this pass records what it prints. Under the ratified ladder a directory read after 1835 can corroborate that a person attested here was still in Chicago and can print a trade or a street the 1835 record never had; on its own it makes nobody a resident of 1835. Nothing on this person's 1835 record was regraded, moved, dated or given an occupation by this entry.
